easy.q: When Elder Dube was a young missionary, why did President Oaks ask that the sign on the mission office gate be taken down?
options: So that no one would feel shut out
Because the sign was old and broken
Because the gate was being replaced
easy.why: The sign warned trespassers away. President Oaks asked that it be removed “to avoid any impression of exclusion,” because we invite all to come unto Christ.

easy.q: What did Elder Dube teach about being perfect and coming to Christ?
options: We must be perfect before we come to Him
We come to Christ to be perfected
We can make ourselves perfect by trying hard
easy.why: Elder Dube said, “We do not need to perfect ourselves to come to Christ. We come to Christ to be perfected.”

easy.q: On the way to the airport, Elder Dube visited Brother and Sister Child. What did he invite them to do?
options: Come to church the very next Sunday
Read the Book of Mormon every day
Choose a date to be sealed in the temple
easy.why: He asked them to “go find a quiet room and choose a date to be sealed in the house of the Lord.” Two months later they were sealed.

easy.q: Elder Dube felt nervous about visiting Brother Child. What did he ask Heavenly Father for?
options: Words to say
More time before his flight
Someone else to go instead
easy.why: He did not know what to say, so while he was on his way he pleaded, “please put words in my mouth.”

easy.q: At the end of his talk, what did Elder Dube invite all of us to do?
options: Write our testimony in a journal each night
Find one person and invite him or her to come unto Christ
Learn one new scripture by heart each week
easy.why: His invitation was to find one person and invite him or her to come unto Christ, or to invite a friend to meet with the missionaries.

medium.q: Elder Dube drew three truths from Moroni’s invitation. What did he say the word “come” teaches?
options: It is a feeling that arrives once we are ready
It is a promise that we will never need to change
It is an action: we choose to move to a better place
It is a call meant mainly for those new to the Church
medium.why: He taught, “Come: It’s an action. We choose to move from our current place to a better place.” Coming to Christ is something we choose to do.

medium.q: According to Elder Dube, what does it mean to “deny yourselves”?
options: To surrender and let go of what is holding us back
To give up every comfort and enjoyment in life
To stop thinking about our own needs at all
To keep our weaknesses hidden from other people
medium.why: Elder Dube explained it in one word, “Surrender,” and added, “Let go of the things that are holding us back.”

medium.q: Sister Child prayed all night for her husband. What answer did she say came to her in the early morning?
options: He must quit smoking before he could be sealed
She should stop worrying and let him work it out
The answer would come later through their leaders
He doesn’t need to be perfect, only to do his very best
medium.why: She said the answer came very clearly: “Randall doesn’t need to be perfect. He needs to do the very best he can.”

medium.q: Elder Dube said the adversary wants to hang the “Trespassers” sign on the gate of our heart. What does the adversary tell us?
options: That the things holding us back are not real problems
That the things holding us back make us unworthy to come
That we can overcome what holds us back by ourselves
That everyone else has already overcome such things
medium.why: Of addiction, doubt, pride, pain, grief, guilt and whatever else holds us back, the adversary “tells us this makes us unworthy to come unto Christ.” The Savior invites us anyway.

medium.q: Elder Dube quoted President Nelson’s teaching that “perfection is pending.” When did President Nelson say it can come in full?
options: In this life, through steady daily effort
As soon as we are baptized and confirmed
Only after the Resurrection, through the Lord
When we make covenants in the temple
medium.why: President Nelson taught that perfection “can come in full only after the Resurrection and only through the Lord.” So we need not have it before we come to Christ.

hard.q: In explaining “be perfected in Him,” how did Elder Dube relate our part to the Savior’s part?
options: We make our hearts new; He then accepts our offering
We come as we are; He asks no change of heart from us
We wait for a new heart; He then invites us to come
We come as we are, willing; He gives us a new heart
hard.why: Elder Dube taught, “Come as we are with a willing heart. He will give us a new heart.” We bring willingness; the change of heart is the Savior’s gift.

hard.q: After telling of the Childs, Elder Dube said, “And that is why President Oaks had the sign on the gate taken down.” What links their story to the sign?
options: A personal visit can succeed where a posted warning has failed
The Church should ask less of those who are still struggling
Coming to Christ is easier for those with a spouse who prays
No one has to overcome what holds them back before coming to Christ
hard.why: Brother Child “didn’t perfect himself to come to Christ.” The adversary says whatever holds us back “makes us unworthy to come unto Christ,” but that warning sign does not belong on the gate.

hard.q: In Elder Dube’s summary of the Childs’ story, what helped Brother Child let go of what was holding him back?
options: His wife’s insistence that he become perfect
The Savior, through His grace
The pressure of a firm temple date
Years of practiced self-discipline
hard.why: Elder Dube said Randall came “with prayer, with trust, and with a willing heart,” and that “the Savior, through His grace, helped him to let go of what was holding him back.”

hard.q: A former missionary wrote that his testimony “is not as certain as it once was.” How did Elder Dube respond to him and to all who feel that ache?
options: He counseled waiting until certainty returns
He listed answers to the hardest questions
He invited them to come unto Christ and embrace His promise
He reminded them of promises they made as missionaries
hard.why: He said, “I invite you, please come unto Christ and embrace His promise,” the promise that the Savior’s joy might remain in us and our joy be full.

hard.q: Which person best fits what Elder Dube promised about losing ourselves in helping someone come unto Christ?
options: Ana waits to share the gospel until her own troubles are settled
Ben studies alone until every one of his doubts is resolved
Cara, though burdened herself, invites a friend to meet the missionaries
Dan decides his problems make him the wrong person to invite anyone
hard.why: Elder Dube promised that as you lose yourself in helping someone come unto Christ, “you will find solutions to your current problems.” We need not wait until our own burdens are gone.
